```{julia}
#| include: false
# Shared setup for chapters that run on Quarto's native julia engine, pulled in
# with Quarto's include shortcode right after the chapter title. Such
# chapters declare in their frontmatter:
#   engine: julia
#   julia:
#     exeflags: ["--project=julia/BookNotebook"]
# Their Julia cells run in julia/BookNotebook (which holds AIInAction), and their
# {python} cells run through PythonCall in the interpreter the rest of the book
# uses (QUARTO_PYTHON, else the project .venv). See julia/BookNotebook/README.md.
let py = get(ENV, "QUARTO_PYTHON",
             joinpath(pwd(), ".venv", Sys.iswindows() ? joinpath("Scripts", "python.exe") : joinpath("bin", "python")))
    ENV["JULIA_CONDAPKG_BACKEND"] = "Null"
    ENV["JULIA_PYTHONCALL_EXE"] = py
    ENV["MPLBACKEND"] = "Agg"   # never open windows; figures go to the page
end
import Pkg
Pkg.instantiate(; io = devnull)
using PythonCall
# Each cell gets its own captured stderr, closed when the cell ends. A logging
# handler created in one cell (as transformers and many libraries do) would keep
# writing to that closed stream from later cells. Make handlers created without an
# explicit stream always write to whatever sys.stderr is current.
pyexec("""
import logging as _logging, sys as _sys
class _CurrentStderr:
    def write(self, s):
        return _sys.stderr.write(s)
    def flush(self):
        try:
            _sys.stderr.flush()
        except Exception:
            pass
_orig_stream_handler_init = _logging.StreamHandler.__init__
def _stream_handler_init(self, stream=None):
    _orig_stream_handler_init(self, _CurrentStderr() if stream is None else stream)
_logging.StreamHandler.__init__ = _stream_handler_init
# joblib's default process pool cannot start workers from an interpreter embedded in
# Julia (they fail to unpickle their tasks and the call hangs). Use threads instead:
# scikit-learn's estimators release the GIL in their compiled code, so n_jobs still
# runs in parallel, and results do not depend on the backend.
try:
    import joblib as _joblib
    _joblib.parallel_config(backend="threading").__enter__()
except Exception:
    pass
""", Main)
# Under the Jupyter engine, plt.show() hands each open figure to the notebook.
# Do the same here: display every open figure through Quarto, then close it.
let plt = pyimport("matplotlib.pyplot")
    plt.show = pyfunc(function (args...; kwargs...)
        for num in plt.get_fignums()
            fig = plt.figure(num)
            display(fig)
            plt.close(fig)
        end
        return nothing
    end)
end
```
